glossary.chronic pancreatitis: Long-term inflammation that scars the pancreas and can cause pain, diabetes and steatorrhoea.
glossary.diabetes mellitus: Raised blood glucose from lack of insulin or resistance to it.
glossary.late-onset diabetes: Diabetes first appearing in later life, here over 50, which can be a sign of pancreatic cancer.
glossary.dark urine: Urine darkened by conjugated bilirubin, typical of obstructive jaundice.
glossary.pale stools: Clay-coloured faeces because bile pigment is not reaching the gut.
glossary.palpable: Able to be felt on examination.
glossary.gallbladder: Small sac under the liver that stores and concentrates bile.
glossary.pancreatic duct: Duct carrying digestive enzymes from the pancreas to the duodenum.
glossary.common bile duct: Duct carrying bile from the liver and gallbladder to the duodenum.
glossary.liver metastases: Cancer that has spread to the liver.
glossary.malnutrition: Poor nutrition from not eating or absorbing enough.
glossary.VTE: Venous thromboembolism: a clot in a vein (DVT) or one that travels to the lungs (PE).
glossary.duodenal obstruction: Blockage of the duodenum, causing vomiting after meals.
glossary.histological: Based on looking at tissue under the microscope.
glossary.biopsy: A small tissue sample taken for examination under the microscope.
glossary.staging: Working out how far a cancer has spread, to plan treatment.
glossary.LFTs: Liver function tests: blood tests of bilirubin and liver enzymes.
glossary.bilirubin: Yellow breakdown product of haemoglobin, cleared in bile.
glossary.sensitivity: How good a test is at picking up people who have the disease.
glossary.specificity: How good a test is at being negative in people without the disease.
glossary.high-resolution CT: A detailed CT scan with thin slices.
glossary.resectable: Able to be removed completely by surgery.
glossary.locally advanced: Grown into nearby structures but not spread to distant organs.
glossary.metastatic: Spread to distant parts of the body.
glossary.opioid analgesia: Pain relief with opioids such as morphine.
glossary.nutritional support: Help with diet, supplements or feeding to prevent weight loss.
glossary.exocrine: Glands that release secretions into ducts, such as pancreatic digestive enzymes.
glossary.ductal epithelium: The layer of cells lining the pancreatic ducts.
glossary.lymphovascular invasion: Tumour cells growing into lymph vessels or blood vessels, a route for spread.
glossary.post-hepatic: Caused by a problem after the liver, in the bile ducts.
glossary.duodenum: First part of the small intestine, where bile and pancreatic juice enter.
glossary.hypercoagulable: Blood more likely to clot than normal.
glossary.tissue factor: A protein that starts the clotting cascade; tumours can release it.
glossary.mucin: Sticky glycoprotein made by some tumours that can trigger clotting.
glossary.islet cell: Hormone-making cells of the pancreas, including insulin-producing beta cells.
glossary.VTE risk: Higher chance of developing a blood clot in a vein.
